key_insight: PSD-based machine learning and end-to-end deep learning both distinguished Rett syndrome from healthy controls, highlighting delta/theta activity and centro-frontal regions as candidate EEG biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: These findings support further research into interpretable EEG tools for Rett syndrome assessment, but do not establish clinical diagnostic readiness.
method: Compared SVM, Random Forest and XGBoost using EEG power spectral density features.
Tested ShallowConvNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet and EEG Conformer on preprocessed EEG signals.
Used SHAP and occlusion sensitivity to interpret model predictions.
evidence_signal: Resting-state, eyes-closed EEG was evaluated with subjectwise cross-validation and balanced accuracy; Random Forest led classical models, EEGNet led deep learning, and 4-second epochs offered the best reported trade-off.
watch_item: The abstract reports neither cohort size nor numerical performance, limiting assessment of reliability and generalizability.
paper_title: EEG Biomarkers for Rett Syndrome: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Explainable AI
